newsitem.title: LATVIA: ESTONIA'S RAKVERE SEES SALES OF 3-5 TONNES A DAY.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA'S RAKVERE SEES SALES OF 3-5 TONNES A DAY.

text.p: Rakvere meat plant, the biggest meat processor in Estonia, said on Friday it sees sales of three to five tonnes a day on the Latvian market through its local warehouse-sales point, opened in Riga in this month.
"We plan to sell some three to five tonnes a day and frankfurters will make up the biggest part of our volume," Maris Kublinsh, the company's manager in Latvia, told a news conference.
"If we are succesful, I would expect meat product prices to go down in Latvia," Hindrek Haarde, acting commercial manager, said.

The company said it needed a local wholesale base to take care of customs and transport procedures which caused a nuisance to its Latvian clients during initial sales from Estonia in the first four months of this year.
Rakvere earlier told Reuters it plans to export 30 to 40 tonnes a week by the end of 1997 to Latvia, Lithuania and St. Petersburg.
Its 1996 production level reached 180,000 tonnes and eight percent was exported.
"We want to increase our export volume significantly this year," Haarde said.
Rakvere has invested one million kroons in Latvia already and plans to increase the figure by the end of the year, Haarde said, but he declined to give a specific figure.
The company's Riga warehouse has a capacity of 10 tonnes.

Haarde said that he expects a growth of meat consumption in the Baltic and CIS countries as purchasing power increases, especially in comparison to Western countries where growth has virtually stopped.
